title: Inspect and extend: A service-shaped simulation
objective: Use the real implementation in `src/exposure.ts` to demonstrate and safely improve exposureservice interface, simulated implementation, and simulation labelling.
problem: A service interface is a plug shape. The current plug is a simulator that returns configured outcomes. Trace its implementation to checkStatusLabel and the status UI so a clear result cannot be mistaken for a real scan. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `src/exposure.ts` and the related project files: src/exposure.ts; src/screens/StatusScreen.tsx.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to exposureservice interface, simulated implementation, and simulation labelling.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: No Bluetooth, Apple/Google exposure notification, diagnosis, or contact-tracing integration exists.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: A service interface is a plug shape. The current plug is a simulator that returns configured outcomes. Trace its implementation to checkStatusLabel and the status UI so a clear result cannot be mistaken for a real scan.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `src/exposure.ts`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
